content.text:
<user>
Return the next passage of fiction.

Afterward I spend an hour walking in the gardens on my own. I do not seek anyone out.
</user>

summary: **Planning quiet garden walk route and NPC presence**
**Integrating subtle garden and east wing details**

item.text:
You leave the dueling grounds by a pale gravel path behind the chapel. The noise of the spectators diminishes as soon as the garden walls rise around you.

The gardens are arranged less like a single design than a long argument conducted in soil. Heat-loving crimson flowers crowd the black demon stone. White lilies grow from a channel of water cold enough to mist in the afternoon air. Farther on, living elven arches have been trained together so slowly that trunks and branches form seamless doorways.

You walk without company.

Students occupy distant benches or cross between Academy buildings, but no one approaches. Behind one hedge, two Commerce students dispute freight tariffs. Their voices fade as the path bends toward the outer terrace.

Here the wall stands low enough to reveal the perpetual storm below. Clouds turn slowly three hundred feet beneath the plateau, lit from within by silent veins of lightning. One of the hard-light bridges stretches eastward above them, bright enough to cast narrow shadows across the flowers.

The path descends again through an orchard bearing blossoms and ripe fruit on the same branches. Brass plaques give planting dates extending back more than two centuries. Several trees are older than Garvey House.

Near the garden’s far end, a narrower walk passes the abandoned east wing. Dust films the windows behind their shutters. A plain door sits beneath dead ivy with a weathered notice fixed beside it:

**MAINTENANCE PENDING — NO ENTRY**

The gravel before it holds no recent footprints. You continue along the curving path without trying the door.

The final quarter of the hour takes you past sheltered ponds, herb beds, and a circular court where blue flowers turn slowly toward the warmth of anyone passing. By the time the tower bell marks the hour, you have looped back to the steps below Garvey House.

The dueling crowd has dispersed. Wind moves through the upper branches, and the garden gate remains open behind you.
